input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS crypto module inventory for serving-stack images (KServe, serving data plane, Platform Operator)

## Description

This epic produces a complete, auditable inventory of cryptographic modules
linked into every image in the model serving stack — KServe components, the
serving data plane, and the Platform Operator image — classifying each module
as validated or non-validated under FIPS 140-3 and recording where each is
used in the request path. The inventory is the factual foundation for all
downstream FIPS remediation, CI enforcement, and certification evidence work,
and is itself a required component of the compliance evidence package.

The epic is anchored to the KServe component and the RHOAI Serving team as
the coordinating owner; its inventory scope deliberately spans the full
serving stack, including the Platform Operator image, so the deliverable
remains a single logical audit artifact rather than one fragment per
component.

## Scope

- Enumerate all container images shipped by the serving stack (KServe
  components, serving data plane images, Platform Operator image).
- For each image, identify all linked cryptographic libraries and modules
  (direct and transitive), including base-image and language-runtime crypto.
- Classify each module as FIPS 140-3 validated or non-validated, citing the
  validation record where one exists.
- Record which modules are exercised in the inference request path versus
  ancillary paths (startup, metrics, tooling).
- Document the full inventory in a reviewable artifact suitable for inclusion
  in the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every serving-stack image is covered by the inventory; none are missing.
- Each crypto module carries a validated/non-validated classification with a
  citable source for the claim.
- The request-path versus ancillary-path distinction is recorded per module.
- The inventory artifact is complete enough that a third party can determine
  which images require remediation without re-deriving the analysis.
- The classification criteria are documented precisely enough to be encoded as
  a machine-readable allow/deny list for CI enforcement.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): the module inventory is an explicit component of the compliance
  evidence package.
- HLR-1 (P0): the inventory defines which images and modules block
  FIPS-enabled-cluster correctness.

# Remediate KServe and serving data plane images to validated crypto modules

## Description

This epic rebuilds the KServe and serving data plane images so that all
cryptographic operations in the inference request path use FIPS 140-3 validated
modules, and verifies that the rebuilt images run correctly on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters.

## Scope

- Replace or rebuild each non-validated crypto dependency flagged by the FIPS
  crypto module inventory in KServe components and serving data plane images,
  prioritizing request-path usage.
- Adjust base images, language-runtime settings, and build configuration so
  validated crypto modules are linked and actually used at runtime.
- Verify remediated images on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters: inference
  requests succeed end to end with validated crypto in the request path.
- Produce build attestations and test results for the remediated images,
  suitable for inclusion in the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All KServe and serving data plane images run correctly on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster: models deploy and serve inference requests successfully.
- No non-validated crypto library is linked in the inference request path of
  any serving image.
- Build attestations and test results for each remediated image are recorded
  and available as certification evidence.
- Any request-path dependency that cannot be remediated is explicitly
  documented with its blocking reason and owner.
- Rollback: because this epic ships rebuilt images rather than replacing a
  running system, the prior image tags remain deployable; reverting a
  deployment to the pre-remediation tag restores the previous behavior on a
  FIPS-enabled cluster without additional migration steps.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules.
- HLR-2 (P0, supporting): produces the build attestations and test results the
  evidence package requires.

# Remediate Platform Operator image to validated crypto modules

## Description

This epic remediates the Platform Operator image so that its cryptographic
operations use FIPS 140-3 validated modules, aligned with the same FIPS posture
as the rest of the model serving stack, and verifies it on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters.

## Scope

- Replace or rebuild non-validated crypto dependencies flagged by the FIPS
  crypto module inventory in the Platform Operator image.
- Adjust base image, language-runtime settings, and build configuration so
  validated crypto modules are linked and used at runtime.
- Verify the remediated operator on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster: it
  reconciles serving resources correctly (creation, readiness, and deletion of
  serving workloads).
- Produce build attestations and test results for the remediated image,
  suitable for inclusion in the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Platform Operator image runs correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift
  cluster and successfully manages the serving stack lifecycle.
- No non-validated crypto library is linked in the operator's request/reconcile
  path.
- Build attestations and test results are recorded and available as
  certification evidence.
- Any dependency that cannot be remediated is explicitly documented with its
  blocking reason and owner.
- Rollback: because this epic ships a rebuilt image rather than replacing a
  running system, the prior Platform Operator image tag remains deployable;
  reverting the operator deployment to the pre-remediation tag restores the
  previous reconciliation behavior without additional migration steps.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): serving-stack images (including the operator that deploys them)
  run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules.
- HLR-2 (P0, supporting): contributes build attestations and test results to
  the evidence package.

# CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions

## Description

This epic adds a gating CI check that fails any serving-stack build which
reintroduces non-validated crypto usage, locking in the FIPS remediation and
preventing regressions.

## Scope

- Implement a build-time or post-build check that scans serving-stack images
  (KServe components, serving data plane, Platform Operator) for non-validated
  crypto usage, driven by the validated/non-validated module classification
  produced by the FIPS crypto module inventory.
- Wire the check into the existing build pipelines as a gating step so a
  failing check blocks the affected build.
- Define the failure output so it identifies the offending module and image.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A build that reintroduces a non-validated crypto module into any
  serving-stack image fails the gating check.
- A clean build (validated crypto only) passes the check.
- The check is enforced as gating, not advisory, in the serving-stack build
  pipelines.
- The classification the check encodes stays in sync with the FIPS crypto
  module inventory.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): CI enforces FIPS regressions — a gating check fails any
  serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

# Compliance evidence package assembly and submission to certification lab

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model
serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and
shepherds it through the mandatory security review board sign-offs and
submission to the external accredited certification laboratory.

## Scope

- Assemble the evidence package from the module inventory, per-image build
  attestations, and test results of the remediated serving stack.
- Structure the package to the certification laboratory's submission
  requirements.
- Present the package at the defined security review board milestones and
  obtain the mandatory sign-offs.
- Submit the package to the external accredited laboratory and track it
  through the certification process.
- Manage remediation requests from the lab or review board until certification
  is granted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the complete module inventory, build
  attestations, and test results for every serving-stack image in scope.
- All defined security review board milestone sign-offs are recorded.
- The package is submitted to the external accredited certification laboratory.
- Responses from the review board or laboratory are triaged and either
  resolved with evidence or routed as follow-up work with owners.
- Note: laboratory turnaround (historically six to nine months) and
  review-board cadence are externally controlled and are schedule constraints,
  not completion criteria for engineering work.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a compliance evidence package is assembled and submitted through
  the security review board to the external certification lab.

# Document FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites

## Description

This epic authors the documentation describing the FIPS support posture of the
model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it on
FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.

## Scope

- Write documentation stating the FIPS 140-3 support posture of the serving
  stack, including what is validated and what is pending certification.
- Document cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation (cluster settings,
  component configuration requirements).
- Include guidance for verifying FIPS operation and for interpreting the CI
  regression check failures.
- Publish through the standard documentation content process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving
  stack accurately, matching the delivered implementation.
- Cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation are documented and
  actionable.
- Content is technically reviewed against the implementation (remediation,
  CI enforcement, and certification status) before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9013 (FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack)

## Triage Outcome

Not below-threshold: the strategy spans two components (KServe, Platform Operator),
multiple distinct work streams (image remediation, CI enforcement, compliance
evidence assembly and external submission, documentation), and a large share of
the schedule is dominated by external/human gates (accredited laboratory
certification with six-to-nine month turnaround, mandatory security review board
sign-off) that are not AI-implementable. Not docs-only: code and image changes
are required. Full decomposition follows.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Component | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|-----------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 | FIPS crypto module inventory for serving-stack images (KServe, serving data plane, Platform Operator) | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | KServe | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | Remediate KServe and serving data plane images to validated crypto modules | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | KServe | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | Remediate Platform Operator image to validated crypto modules | Implementation | RHOAI Platform | Platform Operator | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | KServe | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E005 | Compliance evidence package assembly and submission to certification lab | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | Model Serving Stack | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E006 | Document FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Serving | Documentation | P0 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 Inventory] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 KServe remediation]
    E001 --> E003[RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 Operator remediation]
    E001 --> E004[RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 CI gating check]
    E001 --> E005[RHAISTRAT-9013-E005 Evidence package and submission]
    E002 --> E005
    E003 --> E005
    E001 --> E006[RHAISTRAT-9013-E006 Documentation]
    E002 --> E006
    E003 --> E006
    E004 --> E006
    E005 --> E006
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | 13 (artifact consumer) | The module inventory identifies which images and libraries must be remediated; the remediation builds directly against it. |
| E001 → E003 | 13 (artifact consumer) | Same inventory defines the Platform Operator remediation scope and validated-module targets. |
| E001 → E004 | 13 (artifact consumer) | The CI check encodes the validated/non-validated module classification produced by the inventory; without it the pass/fail criteria are undefined. |
| E001 → E005 | 13 (artifact consumer) | The module inventory is an explicit component of the compliance evidence package (HLR-2). |
| E002 → E005 | 13 (artifact consumer) | Build attestations and test results for remediated KServe/data-plane images are required inputs to the evidence package. |
| E003 → E005 | 13 (artifact consumer) | Build attestations and test results for the remediated operator image feed the evidence package. |
| E001..E005 → E006 | 11 (docs-authoring last) | Documentation describes what was built; it is blocked by all Implementation epics in the strategy. |
| E002 ∥ E003 | 14 (different repos) | Remediation happens in different repos/components with no shared artifacts; parallel. |
| E004 ∥ E002/E003 | 15 (same/different repo, different areas) | The CI check is developed against the inventory classification, not against completed remediation; it runs in parallel with remediation work. |
| E004 ∥ E005 | — | HLR-3 (P1) is regression prevention, not a stated prerequisite for the P0 submission; kept parallel so P0 certification work is not serialized behind P1 work. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epics |
|-----|----------|-------|
| HLR-1 (images run on FIPS-enabled clusters with validated crypto) | P0 | E002, E003 (scope input from E001) |
| HLR-2 (compliance evidence package assembled and submitted) | P0 | E001 (module inventory), E005 (assembly and submission) |
| HLR-3 (CI enforces FIPS regressions with gating check) | P1 | E004 |
| HLR-4 (documentation of FIPS support posture and prerequisites) | P2 | E006 |

All HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Key Decomposition Decisions

- **No Investigation epics.** The strategy's Open Questions section states "None
  on scope". The crypto module inventory ("several images" link non-validated
  crypto) is not a genuine unknown that changes which epics exist — the
  remediation, CI, and evidence epics exist and proceed the same way regardless
  of which specific images are flagged (failure = fix-and-retry). The inventory
  is also a mandatory deliverable of HLR-2, so it is modeled as an
  Implementation epic producing an artifact (Rule 13 serial edges), not an
  Investigation.
- **Platform Operator treated as an existing component.** It is a canonical
  RHAI Jira component (present in `.context/rhai-components.txt`) and the
  strategy references its existing images being remediated, not provisioned.
  However, it has no architecture-context file (only `kserve.md` exists for this
  stack), so its FIPS posture cannot be validated against architecture context —
  see Health Warnings. No repo-onboarding chain was generated because the
  strategy does not introduce a new component.
- **Component/team assignments.** KServe is owned by RHOAI Serving per
  `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`. The strategy
  contains no Impacted Teams table, so the Platform Operator epic is assigned to
